claim: A code verifier is 43 to 128 unreserved characters: letters, digits, hyphen, period, underscore and tilde.
RFC 7636 recommends 32 random octets, base64url-encoded into a 43-character verifier.
quote: The octet sequence is then base64url-encoded to produce a 43-octet URL safe string to use as the code verifier.

claim: A client that can use S256 must use it.
quote: If the client is capable of using "S256", it MUST use "S256"

claim: code_challenge_method defaults to plain when it is left out.
quote: OPTIONAL, defaults to "plain" if not present in the request.

claim: A client must not downgrade to plain after trying S256.
quote: Clients MUST NOT downgrade to "plain" after trying the "S256" method.

claim: Appendix B's example challenge for that verifier.
A verifier that does not match the challenge is answered with invalid_grant.
